content.value_statement: Static pages can struggle to explain complex stories or product journeys. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code design scroll animations, parallax sections, sticky panels, and accessible narrative flows.
actual_capabilities: Compares scroll animation library options such as GSAP ScrollTrigger, Framer Motion, Locomotive Scroll, Lenis, and CSS scroll-timeline.
Shows patterns for parallax layers, sticky sections, horizontal scroll panels, and scroll-triggered reveals.
Provides GSAP, Framer Motion, and CSS examples for scroll-linked motion.
Calls out scroll design anti-patterns such as scroll hijacking, animation overload, and desktop-only experiences.
Highlights sharp edges for jank, mobile parallax, accessibility, and hidden critical content.
limitations: It is guidance-only and does not ship a complete animation library or project scaffold.
Examples are concise and may need adaptation for a specific framework.
It does not include performance profiling scripts or browser test automation.
It does not provide finished visual assets, copywriting, or interaction specs.

use_cases.title: Plan a product feature journey
use_cases.description: Turn product benefits into a scroll sequence with a hook, context, feature reveals, and a final call to action.

use_cases.title: Choose an animation approach
use_cases.description: Compare GSAP, Framer Motion, Lenis, Locomotive Scroll, and native CSS for the project constraints.

use_cases.title: Structure an editorial narrative
use_cases.description: Map story beats, sticky text, visual layers, and reveal timing for a long-form interactive page.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a simple reveal sequence
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a small landing page section.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a simple scroll-triggered reveal sequence for a landing page section. Include the visual order, motion intensity, and accessibility cautions.

prompt_templates.title: Design parallax story beats
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate narrative planning for a marketing or editorial page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a parallax storytelling page with five scroll beats. Include layer roles, scroll depth changes, text reveal moments, and mobile simplifications.

prompt_templates.title: Implement sticky product walkthrough
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to define a sticky product walkthrough with pinned panels, horizontal movement, progress feedback, and fallback behavior for reduced motion users.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a cinematic scroll system
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of an existing experience.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to audit an existing scroll-driven page for jank, scroll hijacking, inaccessible content, mobile breakpoints, and critical content visibility.

output_examples.input: Design a scroll narrative for a new analytics dashboard launch.
output: The page opens with a pinned dashboard preview and a short value statement.
As the user scrolls, metric cards reveal in sequence while the background moves slowly.
The final section releases the pin and presents a direct trial call to action.

output_examples.input: Help choose a scroll animation stack for a React marketing page.
output: Use Framer Motion for lightweight React integration and simple scroll transforms.
Use GSAP ScrollTrigger only for complex timelines or pinned storytelling sections.
Use native CSS view timelines for simple reveals where browser support is acceptable.

output_examples.input: Review a mobile scroll experience that feels slow.
output: Reduce parallax depth on small screens and keep content readable without animation.
Avoid scroll hijacking and preserve natural touch movement.
Check heavy images, pinned sections, and animation count before adding new effects.

best_practices: Keep native scroll behavior and link animation progress to normal scroll movement.
Design mobile and reduced-motion fallbacks before adding complex pinned sections.
Animate key story moments only, so content remains clear and performance stays stable.
anti_patterns: Replacing normal scrolling with forced snap or custom scroll control.
Adding motion to every section without a clear story purpose.
Building effects that hide important content on mobile or reduced-motion settings.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps design scroll-driven pages with parallax, sticky sections, reveals, and narrative pacing.

faq.question: Does it generate production-ready code?
faq.answer: It provides patterns and examples, but teams must adapt and test implementation code.

faq.question: Which animation libraries does it discuss?
faq.answer: It discusses GSAP ScrollTrigger, Framer Motion, Locomotive Scroll, Lenis, and native CSS scroll timelines.

faq.question: Is it useful for mobile experiences?
faq.answer: Yes. It stresses mobile-first design, simpler effects, real device testing, and graceful degradation.

faq.question: Does it cover accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It warns against scroll hijacking, hidden content, and motion patterns that reduce usability.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Designers, frontend developers, and content teams can use it to plan immersive scroll experiences.
